bugs.name: Saving a user's repository limit as 0 resets it to -1
bugs.summary: The report says that in Site Administration > Edit User Account, saving Maximum Number of Repositories as 0 makes the form show -1 when reopened.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that a saved limit of 0 is shown as 0 when the form is reopened.
bugs.actual: After updating a user with a maximum repository count of 0, reopening the edit form was reported to show -1.
reproSteps: In Site Administration, edit a user account.
Set Maximum Number of Repositories to 0 and update the account.
Reopen the edit form and check the value.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: saving 0 keeps 0. Across repeated attempts on a new user and a seeded user, typed and entered by keyboard, the request sent max_repo_creation=0 and the reopened form showed 0 every time; the server passes 0 through unchanged.

bugs.name: Archive queue creates a worker despite maximum workers set to 0
bugs.summary: The report says that after setting the repo-archive queue's maximum number of workers to 0 in Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, requesting a repository archive still starts a worker.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that a maximum of 0 workers prevents any worker from starting.
bugs.actual: After setting the maximum to 0 and downloading a repository ZIP, the queue showed one worker while the maximum still read 0, and the archive was produced.
reproSteps: In Site Administration > Monitor > Queues, open the repo-archive queue and set Max Number of Workers to 0.
Reopen the queue's details and check the number of workers.
bugs.reason: Intended: a maximum of 0 isn't a hard stop. The queue deliberately starts one worker when there are none so queued work is still processed, and Gitea's tests assert that one worker stays.
